title: ACT ON MANAGEMENT OF FIREFIGHTING EQUIPMENT
full_text:
The Act to Partially Amend the Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment, as resolved by the National Assembly, is hereby promulgated.

President Yoon Suk Yeol (Seal)
November 15, 2022
Prime Minister Han Duck-soo
State Council Member and Minister of the Interior and Safety Lee Sang-min

⊙ Act No. 19027
Act to Partially Amend the Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment

The Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment is partially amended as follows.

In the proviso to Article 10 (1), “standard specifications for fire equipment (hereinafter referred to as ‘standard specifications’)” is replaced with “specifications requisite for fire equipment (hereinafter referred to as ‘basic specifications’)”; in paragraphs (2) and (3) of the same Article, “standard specifications” is each replaced with “basic specifications”; in the former part of paragraph (4) of the same Article, “standards” is replaced with “specifications” and “standard specifications” is replaced with “basic specifications”; and in the latter part of that paragraph, “standard specifications” is replaced with “basic specifications”.

In Article 27 (3), “the period of use” is replaced with “the period of use within the maximum period of use determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency for each type of fire equipment”.

In the latter part of Article 35 (1), “the fire equipment maintenance center under Article 36” is replaced with “the fire equipment maintenance center or fire engine maintenance business establishment under Article 36 (1) and (3)”.

Paragraphs (3) and (4) of Article 36 are renumbered as paragraphs (4) and (5), respectively, and the following paragraph (3) is newly inserted in the same Article. In the main clause of the introductory part of paragraph (4) of the same Article (former paragraph (3)), “the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency” is replaced with “the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency or the Mayor/Do Governor”, and “designated as the Center” is replaced with “designated as the Center or designated as a business establishment pursuant to paragraph (3)”. In subparagraph 3 of that paragraph, “paragraph (1)” is replaced with “paragraph (1) or (3)”. In paragraph (5) of the same Article (former paragraph (4)), “the Center” is replaced with “except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), the Center or a business establishment”.
(3) The Mayor/Do Governor may designate an individual or an organization that meets the requirements determined and publicly notified by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, such as professional human resources and facilities, as a fire engine maintenance business establishment (hereinafter referred to as "business establishment") to inspect and maintain fire engines under his or her jurisdiction.

In the introductory part of Article 43, “the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency” is replaced with “the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency or the Mayor/Do Governor”; and in subparagraph 3 of the same Article, “the Center under Article 36 (3)” is replaced with “the Center or a business establishment under Article 36 (4)”.

In the introductory part of Article 45, “Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act” is replaced with “the provisions of Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act”; subparagraph 2 of the same Article is renumbered as subparagraph 3; and the following subparagraph 2 is newly inserted in the same Article.
2. A non-public official member of a special inspection team organized pursuant to Article 21 (2);

Addenda

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the amended provisions of Article 45 shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Applicability to Maximum Period of Use of Fire Equipment)
(1) The amended provisions of Article 27 (3) shall also apply where the procedures for performance confirmation for extending the period of use of fire equipment are under way as at the time this Act enters into force.
(2) Fire equipment whose performance is confirmed for extending the period of use pursuant to the previous Article 27 (3) before this Act enters into force may be used until the extended period of use, notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 27 (3).
Article 3 (Transitional Measures concerning Specifications of Fire Equipment)
The standard specifications determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency pursuant to the proviso of the previous Article 10 (1) before this Act enters into force shall be deemed the basic specifications under the amended proviso of Article 10 (1).

[Partial Amendment]

◇ Reasons for Amendment and Main Provisions

The term “standard specifications” for fire equipment is used to mean specifications that equipment must basically meet where it is used only by fire service agencies or requires special performance for the efficient performance of fire services. The term is therefore changed to “basic specifications” so that its meaning is clear from its name. To ensure the safe use of fire equipment, an extension of its period of use must also remain within the maximum period of use determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency for each type of equipment.

Where a fire equipment maintenance center performing inspections, maintenance, and related tasks is far from a fire service agency, maintenance at a distant location may create gaps in the performance of fire services. Accordingly, a Mayor/Do Governor is permitted to designate individuals or organizations meeting certain requirements as fire engine maintenance business establishments to inspect and maintain fire engines under his or her jurisdiction. These and other changes are intended to remedy shortcomings identified in the operation of the existing system.

<Provided by the Ministry of Government Legislation>
